parakeet: Believe it or not, there are a lot more of us out here. From my experience in nearly two decades of ministry, I've discovered that most of the churches I've engaged were filled with non-believers who simply didn't have the social comfort or the cognitive fortitude to separate from superstitious practices without suffering great cost to their relationships with their families, their friends, and their larger communities. But the big point is that there are people who already no longer believe who are filling the pulpits and the pews of many of our churches. There are entire generations of families who participate without any expectation of supernatural intervention. They only lack the articulation to put words to the cultural and social rationale of their rituals and the permission to dispense with the pretending. The more we raise our voices, the easier it becomes for them to find their own.
